Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Echo CTO), Ben Roy (Staff ML Eng), Dr. Mark Fein (Head Platform)
Recording id: ff-20250918-echo-0007

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
Echo Systems wants to understand Redwood's ability to meet p95 latency SLOs under streaming and high-concurrency token/sec workloads. They want clear numbers for hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) and guidelines for batching/kv cache/quantization tradeoffs. Next: benchmarking window and share of prompt sets, security docs.

Topics: p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, tokens/sec benchmarking, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC networking, SOC2/KMS concerns.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, i'll kick us off. quick intros?
[00:15] Aisha (Echo CTO): hi, aisha here, we run semantics search and a real-time summarization pipeline for call centers, latency is like top constraint for us.
[00:28] Ben (Echo ML): ben — we push streaming tokens, token-per-second is basically the metric, we care about p nine five under load not just average.
[00:42] Marco (Redwood SE): great, marco here — i'm the solutions eng. quick note: when you say streaming, are you using chunked real-time streaming (server-sent events) or long-poll + post-processing?
[00:58] Aisha: chunked streaming, SSE mostly; small chunks ~20-40 tokens per chunk, sometimes bursts of 200 tokens when context flush happens.
[01:12] Dr. Mark: also multi-tenant inside our infra, but for this evaluation we'll test single-tenant traffic patterns first and then go multi-tenant.
[01:28] Lena: okay perfect. can you share target SLOs? e.g., p95 < 300ms for token generation, or p95 < 800ms for full response?
[01:42] Aisha: ideal is p95 sub-400ms per token for the streaming path; for end-to-end responses we can go up to 1.2s for bigger summaries, but steady-state tokens should be low latency.
[01:56] Ben: concurrency wise we expect sustained 200 concurrent streams, spikey to 800 during events. so tokens/sec per worker and batching behaviour matters.
[02:12] Marco: noted. couple of clarifying questions: model size and quantization — are you planning to use an open LLM you host or Redwood-hosted models?
[02:25] Aisha: initially Redwood hosted for speed of rollout, eventually might want dedicated instances or even private VPC for compliance.
[02:36] Marco: ok, good. for hosted vs dedicated we typically see a delta: hosted has more multi-tenant smoothing but sometimes slightly higher p95 in heavy tails; dedicated gives tighter p95 at cost of unit price. we'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[02:50] (transcription glitch) Speaker 6: we — we also want to check kv cash caching and prefix cache, is that supported?
[03:00] Marco: yes KV cache supported, prefix caching too — sorry system sometimes transcribed kv cache as cash in the notes. prefix cache reduces cold-start token work, helpful for repeated prompts.
[03:15] Aisha: can you run an experiment that isolates streaming per-token latency vs batch throughput? we need both.
[03:26] Lena: that's the plan. benchmark windows will include: 1) single-stream sustained token/sec to measure p95 per-token, 2) concurrency ramp (200->800) to measure tail behavior under contention, 3) batching enabled vs disabled to show tradeoffs.
[03:45] Ben: also include kernel-level differences for quantized models — we might accept slight quality loss for a 30% cost improvement.
[03:55] Marco: yes we'll include int8/int4 profiles and note any model-specific artifacts. we'll run token/sec microbenchmarks and end-to-end streaming tests.
[04:09] Aisha: network concerns — when you say private deployment, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, and we have strict egress logging requirements.
[04:22] Marco: Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC with controlled egress; we'll provide network diagrams. note that private/on-prem adds non-trivial network latency depending on colo. we'll measure from your agent locations.
[04:38] Dr. Mark: can we shadow some traffic to compare production vs Redwood hosted in a canary?
[04:46] Lena: yes, canary shadowing is a common pattern. we'll help set that up in the POC if you want.
[04:55] Ben: curious about throttling behavior — if we hit concurrency spikes, do you queue requests, drop, or degrade quality (downscale model)?
[05:06] Marco: Redwood can be configured: queueing with backpressure, automatic fallback to smaller model variants, or reject with 429. we'll show policy options and recommended defaults for low-latency streaming.
[05:20] Aisha: what's typical p95 for streaming token with a 13B quantized model on dedicated? just ballpark.
[05:30] Marco: ballpark: 8-14ms per token for optimized kernels on A100-like hardware at moderate sequence lengths; real numbers depend on sequence length, KV cache hit-rate, and batch size. with smaller GPUs or shared hosted hardware tail can be higher.
[05:47] (noise) Lena: i'll call out that those numbers assume continuous batching and warm kv cache; cold starts multiply the cost/latency.
[05:58] Ben: for our use case we have many short-lived contexts — caching hit rate might be low. does Redwood support warmed persistent sessions / pinned KV?
[06:11] Marco: we support pinned sessions on Dedicated and Private deployments — you can reserve an instance with warm KV. Hosted has ephemeral sessions but we can do longer-lived pods for enterprise customers as a config.
[06:26] Aisha: we need to see p95 under 200 concurrent warm sessions and then at 800 cold sessions.
[06:36] Marco: we'll include both. also we'll capture tokens/sec throughput — e.g., sustained 40k tokens/sec across the cluster vs burst 200k tokens/sec — to see when tail starts to degrade.
[06:50] Lena: rough timeline — if you provide prompts this week we can run an initial bench next week and share results in ~5 business days.
[07:02] Dr. Mark: security checklist — SOC2, SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs, retention and KMS support, can you send an artifact?
[07:13] Lena: yes we'll send our security pack and a short network diagram.
[07:19] (short pause)
[07:25] Ben: what about token accounting — we need per-token cost breakdown across streaming vs batch so product can evaluate pricing models.
[07:36] Marco: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and we can export CSVs. for POC we'll give estimated unit economics for hosted and for dedicated reserved capacity.
[07:50] Aisha: any gotchas with streaming + batching? sounds contradictory.
[07:57] Marco: good question — streaming benefits from small chunks and lower batching. batching helps throughput but increases per-token latency for first tokens. our runtime does continuous batching to try to balance that: immediate dispatch for streaming tokens + opportunistic batching for background tokens. we'll show latency vs throughput curves.
[08:18] Lena: would you like to prioritize end-to-end p95 or cost per 1M tokens?
[08:25] Aisha: end-to-end p95 is primary for Q4 product launch; cost is a secondary metric.
[08:31] Dr. Mark: stakeholders — product (aisha), infra (mark), ml (ben). deciding committee is infra + product. procurement will join after POC if numbers look good.
[08:45] Lena: perfect. any blockers on data sharing?
[08:50] Aisha: we'll anonymize payloads but need an NDA addendum for certain sample traces, can you route that to legal?
[08:58] Lena: yes, i'll loop in legal, we'll attach a narrow NDA amendment.
[09:05] Ben: request — include a test where you intentionally degrade model quantization to see quality drop vs latency gains, we want an ROC-style curve.
[09:16] Marco: good, we'll include int8/int4 and measure token/sec improvement and perplexity/accuracy on your eval set.
[09:28] (background noise, words blurred)
[09:35] Aisha: final question: does Redwood support RPS shaping per-customer in dedicated pools? we want fair sharing across teams.
[09:45] Marco: yes, dedicated pools can be configured with per-tenant quotas, rate limiting and prioritized queues.
[09:53] Lena: ok wrapping — i'll summarize next steps.
[09:57] Lena: action items recap: lena will share benchmark template and security pack; marco will prep hosted vs dedicated delta spreadsheet and test plan; aisha and ben will send representative prompt families and payloads; schedule 2-hour bench window next week.
[10:16] Aisha: that works for us, thanks lena and marco.
[10:21] Dr. Mark: thanks, looking forward to the results.
[10:24] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the calendar invite and the docs.

End of transcript.
